data.about: Eiffel's tower under wind: horizontal loads Q₁…Q₆ act at six storey lines. A trial funicular locates the wind resultant; where it crosses the tower axis, the three-force rule gives the two reaction directions, and their parallels through the ends of the load line meet at the pole o, vertically above the load-line midpoint. Closing the force polygon of every node, storey by storey, shapes both legs: the windward leg resolves in tension, the leeward leg and the horizontal braces (each carrying half a load) in compression — the profile of the built tower follows exactly these funicular curves.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: the tower stands on A and B and rises over six equal storeys (grey lines) to the apex over the middle of the base — drag B or the top C
steps.title: Six storeys over the base A–B

steps.caption: left: horizontal wind loads Q₁ … Q₆ push at the storey lines — right: laid off along a horizontal load line W → E₁, tip to tail
steps.title: The wind loads and the load line

steps.caption: right: any trial pole o′ with rays to the load points — left: between the lines of action, a trial funicular from G₁: one side parallel to each ray
steps.title: A trial funicular

steps.caption: left: the outer trial sides (dashed), extended, meet at M₁: R acts on the horizontal through M₁ (dashed green) — right: R = the whole load line W → E₁, drawn beside it
steps.title: The wind resultant R

steps.caption: left: R crosses the tower axis at O₁; the reactions must point from A and B to O₁ (dashed) — and the axis halves the base: l₁ = l₁ — right: parallels through W and E₁ meet at the pole o
steps.title: O₁ and the pole o

steps.caption: left: the reaction directions carry A (windward, pulled down) and B at the supports — right: A = o→W and B = E₁→o, drawn beside the outer rays
steps.title: The reactions A and B

steps.caption: left: the legs start from A and B toward O₁, up to storey line 1 — right: their forces are the outer rays W–o and o–E₁; o stands vertically above the load-line midpoint: f₁ = f₁
steps.title: Members 1 and 2

steps.caption: left: Q₁ enters the windward node: horizontal brace 3, leg 4 — right: the brace force runs on the horizontal through o and the leg force from Z: they close at T₁, above the midpoint of Z–E₁ (f₂ = f₂), so brace 3 carries Q₁/2
steps.title: Node B₂ — members 3 and 4

steps.caption: right: the leeward node carries no load: its triangle closes with T₁–E₁ — left: leg 5, parallel to it, continues to storey line 2
steps.title: Node G₂ — member 5

steps.caption: left: Q₂ enters at C₂: brace 6, legs 7 and 8 — right: brace force T₁–U₁ = Q₂/2 on the horizontal, leg forces A₁–U₁ and U₁–E₁
steps.title: Storey 2 — members 6, 7, 8

steps.caption: left: Q₃ enters at D₂: brace 9, legs 10 and 11 — right: U₁–W₁ = Q₃/2; every leeward force radiates from E₁, every windward force from a load point
steps.title: Storey 3 — members 9, 10, 11

steps.caption: left: Q₄ enters at E₂: brace 12, legs 13 and 14 — right: W₁–Z₁ = Q₄/2; the legs lean more the higher the storey
steps.title: Storey 4 — members 12, 13, 14

steps.caption: left: brace 15 (= Q₅/2), then both legs meet at the apex where Q₆ enters — right: the triangle D₁–A₂–E₁ closes the tip
steps.title: The apex — members 15, 16, 17

steps.caption: right: the reactions A and B return beside the outer rays: loads + A + B close the force polygon — left: the whole tower stands in equilibrium on A and B
steps.title: The polygon closes

steps.caption: behind: the photograph of the built tower — the windward leg resolves pink = tension, the leeward leg and the braces blue = compression (pipes ∝ force); drag B, C, W, the loads — or click a node for its equilibrium
steps.title: Tension and compression
